'''Mikel J. Harry ''' (born: December 28, 1951; died: April 15, 2017) was a prolific author<ref>{{cite news |title=Control Charts: Keep It Simple |url=https://www.qualitydigest.com/inside/lean-column/control-charts-keep-it-simple-121818.html |publisher=Qualityd Digest |date=December 18, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Meet the man who trained Jack Welch |url=http://mikelharry.indiatimes.com/ |website=[[Indiatimes.com]] |accessdate=14 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Steve Jobs – Yogananda Paramahansa Link Unraveled |url=https://siliconeer.com/current/steve-jobs-yogananda-paramahansa-link-unraveled/ |publisher=siliconeer.com |date=June 9, 2018}}</ref> who is credited for developing [[Six Sigma]], along with [[Bill Smith (Motorola engineer)|Bill Smith]].{{citation needed|date=December 2019}} Harry was sometimes referred to as the 'father of Six Sigma'.{{citation needed|date=December 2019}} One of his books, ''Six Sigma: The Breakthrough Management Strategy Revolutionizing the World’s Top Corporations'' (published by [[Crown Business]], 2000) has been on the bestseller list of [[The Wall Street Journal]], [[Bloomberg Businessweek]] and [[Amazon.com]].<ref name=A/>  He graduated with a PhD from Mary Lou Foulton Teachers College.  

At the age of 65, he died on 25 April 2017, in [[Chandler, Arizona]].<ref name=A>{{cite news |title=Six Sigma Pioneer Mikel Harry Dies at 65 |url=https://www.qualitydigest.com/inside/six-sigma-news/six-sigma-pioneer-mikel-harry-dies-65-042617.html |publisher=Quality Digest |date=April 26, 2017}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
Mikel J. Harry received the lifetime Engineering Excellence Award from [[Arizona State University]] in 2002.<ref name=A/> He was inducted into the "[[Who's Who]]" Registry of Global Business Leaders in 1993.
